chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says when he exits from the door of his house: 'I seek refuge with that with which the Angels of Allah seek refuge, from the evil of this new day which, when its sun sets, will not return, from the evil of myself, and from the evil of others, and from the evil of the Satans, and from the evil of the one who establishes hostility towards the Guardians of Allah, and from the evil of the Jinn and the humans, and from the evil of the predatory wild animals and the insects, and from the evil of indulging in the Prohibitions, all of them. I pledge myself with Allah from every evil. Allah will forgive him, turn to him, suffice him against worries, hold him back from evil, and protect him from harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house for protection from evil?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication emphasizes the concept of 'Istia'dha' (seeking refuge) by aligning the believer's protection with that of the Angels, a practice rooted in the Shia tradition of daily spiritual armor. It comprehensively covers internal and external threats—from one's own self and Shayatin to enemies of the Awliya—promising divine forgiveness and relief from anxiety as a reward for consistent recitation.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who says when he goes out from the door of his house, ‘I seek Refuge with whatever the Angels of the Lord seek Refuge with, from the evil of this new day which, when its sun sets, will not return, from the evil of myself, and from the evil of others, and from the evil of the Satans<sup>la</sup>, and from the evil of the one who establishes hostility to the Guardians<sup>asws</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and from the Jinn and the human beings, and from the evil of the predatory wild animals and the insects, and from the evil of indulging in the Prohibitions, all of them. I pledge myself with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from every evil, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive (his sins) for him, and Turn to him, and Suffice him for the worries, and Save him from the evil, and Protect him from the evil’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Asim ibn Hamid from abu Basir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever says, when coming out of his door, ‘I seek protection with that by which the angels of Allah seek protection, against the evil of this new day which when it is its sunset it will not come back, I seek protection against the evil of my soul and the evil of the others, I seek protection against Satan and those who are against the friends of Allah, I seek protection against the evil of Jinn, human beings, the beast and the reptiles and against the evil of involvement in all of the unlawful matters and I place myself under the protection of Allah against all evil,’ Allah will forgive him, accept his repentance, suffice him in what is important to him. He will be safeguarded against evil and protected from misfortunes.”
